claims.text: The opportunity supports undergraduate students to develop research skills.
The opportunity involves undertaking a short research project during the summer vacation.
The scholarships are open to students from low-income households.
The scholarships are open to students who are ordinarily resident in Scotland.
The scholarships are open to students enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish institution.
Scholarships are intended to cover recipients' living costs while they undertake research.
Scholarships provide experience and skills in preparation for postgraduate study or the workplace.
Students may see their research results published in academic journals or reported in conference presentations.
Eligibility is determined by an online checker, but the final decision is based on the application form, supporting evidence, and supervisor's statement.
Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland and have been so before beginning their degree.

Applicants must have spent 2 years in full-time secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR have a substantive connection with Scotland on the basis of residency, education (excluding university), family, or working life.
Applicants must reside in a low-income household, with specific income thresholds provided.
Applicants must be undergraduate students at one of the 18 listed eligible Scottish institutions.
Applicants must be enrolled at their institution for the full duration of their degree, or have transferred after completing an HNC/HND from a Scottish college.
Applicants must be in the 3rd year of a 4-year degree, or in the 3rd or 4th year of a 5-year degree, or in the 2nd year of a 3-year degree.
Part-time students must be at an equivalent stage in their course.
Applicants must be entitled to live and work in the UK.
Applicants must have never previously held a Carnegie Vacation Scholarship.
Applicants are not eligible if their permanent home address is outside Scotland.
Applicants are not eligible if they are not an enrolled undergraduate at one of the 18 eligible Scottish institutions.
Applicants are not eligible if they are in the final year of their course and scheduled to graduate in summer 2026.
Applicants are not eligible if they have held a Carnegie Vacation Scholarship in the past.
Applicants are not eligible if their migration status does not entitle them to work in the UK.
Projects must be between 4 and 12 weeks in duration.
Projects must take place between May 12th and August 31st.
Projects must address a clearly specified research question(s) or hypothesis.
Projects must engage the student in personal research over the specified period.
Projects must provide scope to develop ideas, use initiative, and build research and analytical skills.
Projects can be based at the student's home university or another research organization.
Projects that form part of assessed coursework are not eligible.
Projects that are a direct continuation or expansion of an existing/larger project or study are not eligible.
Projects involving participation in group expeditions are not eligible.
Projects consisting solely of a literature review are not eligible.
Work placements (paid or unpaid) or volunteering activities are not eligible.
Attendance of summer schools, language study, or other training courses are not eligible.
Projects must be supervised by an academic member of staff at the student's university.
Supervisors may only nominate a single student per academic year.
Supervisors must confirm their availability and willingness to supervise.
It is the supervisor’s responsibility to ensure the project is completed within the agreed timescale.
Supervisors are expected to liaise with their department for timely distribution of the scholarship.
Supervisors must ensure the student receives adequate training and all statutory requirements are satisfied.
If the project is conducted at a different organization, the home institution supervisor must ensure a suitably qualified host supervisor is available.
Reviewers will assess academic standing, motivation, project quality, and supervision/environment.
Applicants are expected to be on course to achieve a 2:2 or higher classification and Honours where applicable.
The scholarship is intended as a stipend to cover living expenses and accommodation costs.
The stipend is calculated using the Scottish Living Wage rate.
There is no additional funding for consumables, equipment, or overheads.
Host organizations are responsible for ensuring students have access to necessary equipment and consumables.
Applicants state the amount of support in full-time working weeks.
Projects can be completed on a part-time basis, but support is still indicated in full-time weeks.
The online application portal opens approximately 11 weeks before the closing date.
After the student submits their part, an email is sent to the supervisor to complete the application.
The supervisor submits the complete application to the Trust.
Students receive confirmatory emails upon submission and when the supervisor submits their part.
It is recommended to allow at least 5 working days for the supervisor to complete their part of the application.
The scholarships support students from low-income households who are typically unable to take advantage of extra-curricular development opportunities due to financial constraints.
Total household income thresholds are used as a guide for assessing applications.
